1.title: Exam Orientation and How to Study
1.text: Welcome to Module zero: Exam Orientation and How to Study. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. What the exam is. The two skill areas. Where each skill lives in this course. How to read the exam wording. A repeatable way to answer a question. A study plan. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: Both skill areas. Exam format: a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes; check the exam page for the time. Validated against: the official A I nine oh one study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: What the exam is
1.text: What the exam is. The A I nine oh one exam is the current exam for the Microsoft Azure A I Fundamentals certification. It is for people at the beginning of an A I solution development career. You need conceptual knowledge of A I solutions in Azure, foundational technical skills to work with them, Python syntax, and familiarity with Azure resources. Important. The older exam A I nine hundred was retired on June thirty, two thousand twenty-six. If a book, video or practice test says A I nine hundred, its content is out of date: it did not cover building with Microsoft Foundry, which is more than half of A I nine oh one.

1.title: What the exam is, continued
1.text: What the exam is. Passing score. seven hundred or more. Languages. English first; other languages follow about eight weeks later. Retirement date. none announced on the exam page. Duration, number of questions, price. not on the pages this course was built from: confirm on the exam page. The price depends on the country or region. Note. Most questions cover generally available features. The exam may include Preview features if they are commonly used, so read the product names in this course as "current at the time of writing" and check Microsoft Learn before you book. Exam tip: If a study resource says A I nine hundred, it is out of date: the current exam is A I nine oh one, and more than half of it is about building with Microsoft Foundry.

1.title: What the exam is, continued
1.text: What the exam is. The figure shows this: The A I nine oh one exam at a glance: two skill areas and their weights.

1.title: The two skill areas
1.text: The two skill areas. Identify A I concepts and capabilities. Weight: forty to forty-five percent. What it asks: Responsible A I, how generative models work, choosing models and settings, and recognizing A I workloads. Implement A I solutions by using Microsoft Foundry. Weight: fifty-five to sixty percent. What it asks: Prompts, deploying and chatting with a model, the S D K, agents, text and speech, vision and image generation, information extraction. The second area is the bigger one, and it is hands-on in spirit: you must recognize what a small Python program does and which Foundry feature it uses. You do not need to memorize long code.

1.title: Where each skill lives in this course
1.text: Where each skill lives in this course. one, two, three, four, five. Skill area: Concepts and capabilities. Topics: responsible A I; generative models; models and parameters; workloads; capabilities. six, seven, eight, nine. Skill area: Foundry: generative A I and agents. Topics: prompts; portal; S D K chat client; agents. ten, eleven, twelve. Skill area: Foundry: text, speech, vision, extraction. Topics: text and speech apps; vision and image generation; Content Understanding. thirteen. Skill area: Both. Topics: exam technique and final review.

1.title: How to read the exam wording
1.text: How to read the exam wording. Describe. Explain what it is and what it is for. Identify. Pick the right option for a described need. Create. Know the steps or the settings that produce the result. Deploy, build. Recognize the portal steps or the code that does it. Interpret. Read what a request or output means.

1.title: A repeatable way to answer a question
1.text: A repeatable way to answer a question. Read the last sentence first to see what is asked. Find the key need: text, speech, image, document, agent, safety, cost. Name the workload and drop options from other workloads. Pick the most specific service or feature for the need. Read code questions line by line: client creation, the call, the input, the output. Mark and move on if two options remain after a minute.

1.title: A study plan
1.text: A study plan. one. What to do: Learn the ideas: responsible A I, how generative models work, models and parameters. Modules: one to three. two. What to do: Learn the workloads and what each A I capability does. Modules: four to five. three. What to do: Learn Foundry from prompts to agents. Modules: six to nine. four. What to do: Learn the services behind text, speech, vision and extraction. Modules: ten to twelve. five. What to do: Review with the cards and practice questions. Modules: thirteen. Spaced review: answer each module's recall questions from memory, then check. Repeat each Quick Reference Card the next day and again after a week.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors finds a study book for "A I nine hundred" in a shop. What should the team know before using it? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A I nine hundred was retired on June thirty, two thousand twenty-six, and A I nine oh one is the current exam. The study guide states that A I nine hundred was retired on June thirty, two thousand twenty-six. A I nine oh one is the exam for the Azure A I Fundamentals certification.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which skill area carries the larger weight in A I nine oh one? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Implement A I solutions by using Microsoft Foundry, at fifty-five to sixty percent. Implementing A I solutions by using Microsoft Foundry is fifty-five to sixty percent, the larger area.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A candidate reads the skill "Create a lightweight chat client application by using the Foundry S D K". What is expected? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Recognize what a short Python program does and which Foundry feature it calls. The exam checks that you understand small applications and the Foundry features they use, not long memorized code.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. What is the passing score of the A I nine oh one exam? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: seven hundred. A score of seven hundred or greater is required to pass.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which exam replaced A I nine hundred? Answer: A I nine oh one. Question two. Name the two skill areas and their weights. Answer: Identify A I concepts and capabilities (forty to forty-five percent) and Implement A I solutions by using Microsoft Foundry (fifty-five to sixty percent). Question three. What score passes? Answer: seven hundred or more.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which programming language does the exam expect you to read? Answer: Python. Question five. Which part of a question do you read first? Answer: The last sentence. Question six. Can the exam include Preview features? Answer: Yes, if they are commonly used.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Exam: A I nine oh one for Azure A I Fundamentals; A I nine hundred retired June thirty, two thousand twenty-six; pass at seven hundred. Skill areas: concepts and capabilities forty to forty-five percent; implement with Microsoft Foundry fifty-five to sixty percent. Audience: beginning of an A I solution development career; Python syntax and Azure resources. Method: last sentence, key need, name the workload, most specific service, read code line by line, mark and move on. In the next module, we continue the course.
